summary: Oman lets GCC nationals enter freely and waives visas for short visits by around 80 nationalities — including the EU, US, UK and Canada, for stays of up to 14 days — while the Royal Oman Police eVisa covers longer tourist stays; other nationalities need a sponsored or embassy visa.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says credit cards are widely accepted, and Australia's Smartraveller says credit card facilities and ATMs are widely available and that US dollars and euros are easy to exchange at banks and currency bureaus.

safety.text: Attacks on foreigners in Oman are relatively rare, but the FCDO reports strikes and retaliatory attacks by Iran in Oman, among other places in the region, since 8 July 2026, and warns of flight cancellations and short-notice airspace closures. Stay away from military and security sites, respect local laws and customs, and take care in wadis, which flood after heavy rain from October to March.

tips.text: The 14-day visa-free entry is for genuine short visits and formally requires a return ticket, accommodation and health insurance — for longer trips apply for the 30-day eVisa on the Royal Oman Police portal before travel.

The UK FCDO says wadis (dry riverbeds) are prone to flash flooding after heavy rain from October to March. Check the forecast before visiting a wadi and avoid places where heavy rain is expected, and for at least one day afterwards.

The UK FCDO says road trips to the desert and mountains can be dangerous unless you are in a well-equipped four-wheel-drive vehicle; travel in convoy if possible, carry water and a phone, and leave your plans with someone.
The UK FCDO says to dress modestly in public areas, including malls, with the tops of arms and legs (below the knee) covered, and not to wear swimwear in public except on tourist beaches or at pools.

The UK FCDO says visitors can buy and drink alcohol only in licensed venues such as hotels, restaurants and clubs (legal age 21). Drinking or being drunk in public and drink-driving are illegal, and any alcohol found in a driver's system can bring a fine and possible imprisonment.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Oman?
faq.answer: GCC nationals enter freely. Around 80 nationalities — including the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and China — can enter visa-free for up to 14 days, provided they hold a return ticket, accommodation and health insurance. For longer tourist stays the Royal Oman Police issues an unsponsored 30-day eVisa. Other nationalities need a sponsored or embassy visa.

faq.question: How does Oman's 14-day visa-free entry work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationalities are admitted without a visa for stays of up to 14 days at all entry points. The waiver formally requires a confirmed return ticket, an accommodation booking and health insurance. It is intended for single short visits — for anything longer, apply for the eVisa before travel and confirm current eligibility on evisa.rop.gov.om.

faq.question: How much does the Oman eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The unsponsored tourist eVisa costs OMR 5 for a 10-day visit or OMR 20 for 30 days (the stay can be extended by the same length, the first time online). Apply only through the Royal Oman Police portal at evisa.rop.gov.om and confirm the exact fee during the application.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Oman?
faq.answer: Oman has no diplomatic relations with Israel and does not currently admit travelers on Israeli passports. Confirm with an Omani embassy before making any plans, as policy can change.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Oman?
faq.answer: No official source names a best time to visit. The UK FCDO says wadis are prone to flash flooding after heavy rain from October to March, tropical cyclones sometimes affect Oman in July and August, and extreme heat has caused deaths from dehydration and heat exhaustion.
